chapter: Friends, New York life and recording routine
title: Fats Waller, Clarence Williams and Eva Taylor
summary: She went out often with Fats Waller, Clarence Williams was cautious, and she felt sorry for Eva Taylor under Williams's meanness.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Oh, is that when you were friendly with Fats Waller?
Uh-huh. Me and Fats used to go out quite often.
Can you remember anything about Fats that you could tell us for the record?

No. The only thing (unintelligible) he'd come and get me and take me out and I never (unintelligible) about me having a husband. He would get skeptical of talking to me and Clarence Williams (PHONETIC), ________, "Man, don't do this," "Man, don't do that," "Man, don't do --" (Laughter.) "Man, you're going to mess things up." "Man, you're going to --" (Laughter.)
He was saying that to Fats?
Yeah, he says, "Man, you're going to mess things up." "Man, you're going to --"
Was Fats as much fun as he seemed to appear later?
I used to feel so sorry
Yeah. Why did you feel sorry for her?
Because she couldn't enjoy her life because Clarence was so mean to her. I know she wanted to be more lively
Why was he so mean to her? Clarence.
